correctness.rationale: For m,n>=3 the closed neighborhoods leave, for one sensor, an entire row and column and every other observed vertex has m+n-4>=2 missing neighbors; no force. A pair in distinct rows and columns leaves exactly two cross cells, each uniquely forced in one simultaneous round. A set with no nonattacking pair lies wholly in one row or one column; if t>=2 chosen cells in a row, exactly u=n-t cells remain, and forces occur iff u<=2. This proves the exhaustive success classification, disjoint subtractive polynomial, sharp universal threshold max(2,m-2,n-2), and one-step bound. Bernoulli counts give both asymptotic limits. Independent exhaustive adjacency simulation checked 70,141 nonempty sets for (3,3),(3,4),(4,4), including success and number of rounds; these finite cases are corroboration only.
